label: def:interaction-sector-taxonomy
title: Interaction-sector taxonomy
html:
Definition. Interaction-sector taxonomy

Definition (interaction-sector taxonomy). The framework's interactions form three sectors — strong, electromagnetic, and weak — classified by the bar-involution parity of the sector's primary observable, the calibration its scale anchors to, and its coupling object.

Sector Primary observable Bar parity (q \mapsto q^{-1}) Scale anchor Coupling object
strong binding \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}, volume even (cosh channel) E_0 = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}); confinement-SDP duals
electromagnetic Coulomb energy, Hartree scale provably no pure channel (mixed at coupling and observable level) E_h = \alpha_{EM}^2\, m_e c^2 \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q_0\,[9]_q\,[10]_q dressed by the Chern–Simons tower
weak \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} odd (sinh channel) CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, proxy m_\mu/m_e) bar-odd channel of the complex volume

Processes are not sectors: a fusion process is a strand-balanced rearrangement inside the strong sector, while β-decay moves proton number on the subject side and is thereby routed to the weak sector. The bar-even and bar-odd channels are intertwined by the bar involution itself — the rotation between the two channel recurrences of the binding–Q_\beta complex volume conjecture — so the taxonomy's parity column is a statement about where each sector's observable lives, not a wall between algebras.

The Lean formalization records the taxonomy as a total assignment and proves that weak is the unique bar-odd-assigned sector, that strong is the unique bar-even one, and that the electromagnetic sector is exactly the one carrying no pure-parity assignment — which is itself a theorem, not an omission, as follows.

At the coupling level the electromagnetic cell is now derived. The quantum integer [n]_q is bar-even — invariant under q \mapsto q^{-1} — so in the bare coupling C(q) = q\,[9]_q[10]_q only the exponential prefactor moves under the bar involution, giving the exact decomposition

  C(q) \pm C(q^{-1}) \;=\; (q \pm q^{-1})\,[9]_q[10]_q .

The bar-even part of the electromagnetic coupling is the cosh-channel (strong-side) multiple and the bar-odd part the sinh-channel (weak-side) multiple of one invariant factor B = [9]_q[10]_q: the electromagnetic coupling is the full exponential mix e^{\lambda} B with \lambda = \ln q, sitting at the intertwiner point between the two pure channels rather than in either. At the substrate anchor the odd-to-even ratio is \tanh(\ln q_0) \approx 0.10396 exactly for the bare coupling, and \approx 0.10356 for the Chern–Simons-dressed value, whose tower is not bar-covariant in a single parity (\hbar_q^2 \mapsto q^2 \hbar_q^2). The observable level follows: \alpha = C^{-1} carries the conjugate exponential e^{-\lambda} (odd-to-even ratio -\tanh\ln q_0), and the Hartree scale \alpha^2 the doubled e^{-2\lambda} (ratio -\tanh 2\ln q_0 \approx -0.2057). Moreover, under the nondegeneracy that holds at the real anchor (q^2 \neq \pm 1, B \neq 0), the coupling is provably neither bar-even nor bar-odd — the electromagnetic cell is not unassigned but provably admits no pure-parity assignment, in exact contrast to binding (pure even) and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (pure odd). All of this is proved over any field in the library module QOU.Interactions.EmCouplingBarParity; the numeric twin is computations/probes/alpha_em_bar_parity_probe.py.
